about: Sourced ranges for every drive and line figure the model uses (D-040, docs/24-motor-sources.md). Keys under motors are tools/tendon_calc.py MOTORS names; fields are the Motor fields in the same units and convention (stall torque and no-load speed at the gearbox output, stall_torque_nm before the class's gearbox efficiency eta). Each figure has three cases: low = the pessimistic end of that figure (for stall_current_a that is the most amps per newton metre, which costs energy), nom = the best sourced estimate, high = the optimistic end. ROBOT_MOTORS=low|nom|high (tools/export_mjcf.py) runs the model on one case for every drive at once. eta is the gearbox efficiency the model multiplies stall_torque_nm by; it is 1.0 where the source figure is measured or stated at the output with the gearbox losses already in it. Line break_n is the effective strength of the line as terminated (wrapped on the drum and pulley before the crimp), not the spool label.

N20_298:1.part: Pololu 298:1 Micro Metal Gearmotor HP 6V, extended shaft (#2218), 6 V
N20_298:1.notes: Pololu's 2020+ dynamometer datasheet (rev 6.2): 40 kg mm (0.39 N m) stall, extrapolated, measured at the output, so eta 1.0. 0.49 N m is the pre-2020 figure (70 oz in), still on resellers. Low: Pololu says units stall well before the extrapolated point as they heat; taken as 0.8 x (the +-20 % speed tolerance applied to torque). Continuous: Pololu advises 25 % of stall current or less: 0.4 A gives 9.0 kg mm on the measured current line (0.23 of stall); low is the max-efficiency point 6.5 kg mm (0.16); high is the model's 0.30. Gearbox limit 20 kg mm (0.196 N m), instantaneous: keep loads well under it. No measured comparison of no-name N20 298:1 against Pololu was found; vendor claims are 33 to 75 % of Pololu's stall.

N20_100:1.part: Pololu 100:1 Micro Metal Gearmotor HP 6V (#2214); hands and face, not in the model yet
N20_100:1.notes: Pololu rev 6.2: 17 kg mm stall, 310 rpm; low 0.8 x, high the old figure (0.21). Continuous as the 298:1.

JGB37_1:90.part: JGB37-520 12 V 1:90 '110 rpm' (about 10 000 rpm motor) with hall encoder
JGB37_1:90.notes: Seller tables: Hiwonder JGB37-520R90-12 15 kg cm stall at 3.2 A, 2.6 kg cm rated; NFP JGB37-520-12100 12 kg cm stall at 2.4 A, 3.0 kg cm rated, +-15 % speed; RAM e-shop 15 kg cm max at 2.3 A. Hiwonder's 1:90 / 1:30 stall ratio (2.59 for 3) shows its figures carry the gearbox loss, so they are taken at the output (eta 1.0). NFP's table scales stall exactly with ratio (motor x ratio, no loss): low is NFP's 1.18 N m x 0.65 (gearbox efficiency derived from a supplier stall table across ratios and Maxon's 4 to 5 stage spur gearheads, 0.59 to 0.66). Nom 1.10 between the two readings. Continuous: rated torque 0.255 / 0.27 / 0.294 N m (Hiwonder, mid, NFP) as fractions of each case's stall. Mass: NFP 144 to 170 g, Yahboom MD520 150 g; Hiwonder's 200 g is shipping weight. The model's 1.7 N m and 3.5 A are above every source. A 6000 rpm winding sold under the same name gives 66 rpm and 8 kg cm at 1:90: check the listing says 110 rpm.

775_PLAN40.part: 775 brushed, 12 V, rated about 12 000 rpm at 12 V, ball bearing, on a printed two-stage 1:40 planetary
775_PLAN40.notes: Motor x 40. Kt is settled by the speed: 12 000 rpm at 12 V is Kv 1000 rpm/V, Kt = 60 / (2 pi Kv) = 0.0095 N m/A; on nine 775-class sheets (VEX 775pro, AndyMark RedLine, Banebots RS775-18 and -12, Kinmore RS-775PH and RS-770PHF, Techtonics, NFP 775SHP, Handsontec) the stall-point Kt is 0.86 to 1.05 x the speed one. The motor constant Km = Kt / sqrt(R) of those sheets is 0.018 to 0.028 N m/sqrt(W), which with Kt 0.0095 gives R 0.28 / 0.18 / 0.14 ohm, stall current 12 / R = 45 / 66 / 87 A and stall torque Kt (I - I0) = 0.40 / 0.62 / 0.80 N m (Handsontec's 12 000 rpm 775: 0.66 N m at 12 V; RS775-18 at 12 V: 0.80 N m, 86.7 A). So the model's 0.6 N m is right and its 25 A is not: the current at a given torque is 2.6 x the model's. Speed: Handsontec 12 000, RS775-18 at 12 V 13 000, -10 % tolerance (AndyMark). Continuous: no source rates a cheap 775; a stalled 775 tolerates about 11 to 25 W of copper loss (Chief Delphi locked-rotor reports), 8 to 12 A at 0.18 ohm, 15 A with the fan turning: 7 / 10 / 15 A, Kt (I - I0) as fractions of each case's stall. Gearbox: printed two-stage planetary 0.35 / 0.50 / 0.65 (COMPAct dyno: single PLA stage 0.60 to 0.80, compound 14:1 about 0.60; a GitHub 16:1 two-stage about 0.50; squared single stages 0.36 to 0.64). No dynamometer test of a printed 1:40 exists.

WORM_10RPM.part: 12 V worm gearmotor 5840-31ZY class, 58 mm gearbox, 8 mm shaft, 10 rpm 1:634 (Greartisan B07YBXMTWC)
WORM_10RPM.notes: Greartisan: rated 40 kg cm (3.92 N m) at 1.4 A (+-10 %), 1:634. The electrical stall of the 31ZY motor through 1:634 is far above the gear's strength (35 to 42 kg cm per amp, 3.8 to 6.5 A stall: 125 to 220 kg cm), so the usable stall is the gearbox limit: NFP 5840-31ZY-S caps stall at 40 kg cm for every ratio from 54:1, NFP 5840-31ZY-DSH gives 70 kg cm max: low 3.92, high 6.9 N m, nom between. The model's 7.84 N m (twice rated) is above every source. Current at each torque on Greartisan's line (0.25 A + 35 kg cm/A, +10 % at low). Continuous: rated 3.92 N m (low: 75 % of it, in a closed torso, unsourced derating). Figures at the output: eta 1.0. Mass: NFP 360 g, Amazon 13.1 oz (371 g).

5010_PLAN16.part: generic 12N14P 5010 360 KV outrunner (RCTimer / Readytosky class, about 92 g) on FOC at a 20 A driver peak + printed 1:16 planetary, 12 V
5010_PLAN16.notes: Kt per amp of phase-current amplitude = 8.27 / Kv (15 sqrt(3) / pi / Kv, ODrive's torque constant); 9.55 / Kv is per DC (six-step ESC) amp, confirmed within 7 % by T-Motor MN501-S thrust-stand data. Kv +-10 %: Kt 0.0209 / 0.0230 / 0.0255; x 20 A x 16. Resistance: 0.24 ohm measured line to line on a generic 5010 360 KV (SimpleFOC forum), RCTimer 5010 siblings scaled by 1/Kv^2 0.275 to 0.35; the model's 0.15 is below every generic source. The premium 24N28P class (T-Motor MN501-S 360 KV) is 0.045 ohm and 175 g: a different motor. Continuous without airflow: 3 / 6 / 9 A amplitude (SimpleFOC guess 3 A; 6 and 9 A from an assumed 4 to 5 K/W winding-to-air, unsourced). Speed 0.9 Kv V / 16. Gearbox as the 775's printed planetary.

5010_PLAN25_24V.part: the same 5010 on a printed 1:25 planetary, 24 V (6S)

lines.notes: Effective strength = label x line factor x termination factor. Line: branded braid tests 1.04 to 2.0 x label at 20 lb, 1.12 (Sufix 832 40 lb) and 1.26 (50 lb) on Instron; a cheap Chinese '50 lb' 0.86; no tests at 100 or 200 lb: 0.85 / 1.0 / 1.25 x label. Termination: the line wrapped at least three turns round the drum (and round the joint pulley) before its crimp or knot, so the capstan effect leaves 6 to 15 % of the tension at the crimp and the limit is the line bent on the drum at D/d 17 to 40 (HMPE keeps full strength above 8:1): 0.85 / 0.9 / 0.9 x. Low 0.72, nom 0.90, high 1.10 x label. A knot or crimp carrying the full load is 0.3 / 0.5 / 0.75 x label (Sport Fishing Instron knot tests; crimps on bare braid slip, no numbers) and is not allowed: at 0.3 it breaks below the 1/3 clutch.
